newsitem.title: CHINA: PRESS DIGEST - Chinese newspapers - June 12.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Chinese newspapers - June 12.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Chinese political and business stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Beijing. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy. Telephone: (8610) 6532-1921. Fax: (8610) 6532-4978.
PEOPLE'S DAILY
- President Jiang Zemin to attend Hong Kong handover ceremony
- Successful launch of two satellites in one month will have great impact on China's status in international aerospace arena, Premier Li Peng says
- Number of criminals drops 30 percent by end-May while numberof criminals on run drops 20 percent
XINHUA DAILY TELEGRAPH
- Politburo member Hu Jintao urges young experts to do best to understand socialism with Chinese characteristics, and strive to propel opening-up and modernisation into next century.
CHINA SECURITIES
- China Securities Regulatory Commission revokes licence of Jiaxin Futures Co
- Frontpage editorial says bank funds withdrawn from stock market should be used as loans
FINANCIAL NEWS
- Shenzhen stock exchange to freeze short-selling funds
- Northwestern Gansu closes 10 illegal futures companies
- Jiangxi Jinjiang closes one illegal futures company
- State Administration of Foreign Exchange issues business licence to Zhanghong Life Insurance Co
- Bank of China to spend $2.0 million on new Oracle database
- Official of State Administration of State Property says China will select profitable listed firms for listing of state-owned shares, but only at right moment
BEIJING ECONOMIC DAILY
- Beijing sets up 3.0 million military caps factory to make caps for People's Liberation Army stationed in Hong Kong
CHINA DAILY
- President Jiang Zemin urges need for ethnical education in schools
- Retail price inflation falls 0.8 percent year-on-year in May
- Beijing stadium prepares for handover celebration
- World Bank backs $360 million relief programme
- China Great Wall Computer Shenzhen Co Ltd issuing 57 million shares in Shenzhen
